ai.title: Replace NodeJS.Timer with any in websocket-client.ts
ai.summary: Type error in `common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts` resolved by casting `OutstandingTxn.timeout`, `APIRealtimeClient.connectTimeout`, and `APIRealtimeClient.heartbeat` from `NodeJS.Timer` to `any`. The `NodeJS.Timer` type was causing compilation failures in the shared core package. Scope limited to `common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts`.

eli5.text: The app's internal connection helper used a very strict label for its timers that didn't match what the shared code expects, which broke the build. The team swapped that label for a more flexible one, so the connection helper once again lines up with the rest of the shared code and the build passes. If you were watching the developer tools, you'd see the build finish instead of stopping on a type error; there's no change to how the app behaves once it's running.

ai.title: Skip file context update when client used tool
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts now wraps the file context update and prompt cache warming in a `!didClientUseTool(lastMessage)` check. This prevents redundant file selection steps when the last message indicates tool usage. Scope limited to backend main prompt logic. Refactors existing flow to align with tool usage state.

eli5.text: When you asked the assistant to do something using a built-in tool (like searching files), it sometimes unnecessarily re-ran the file selection step. Now the system checks whether your last message already used a tool, and if so, it skips that redundant file-picking step. You would notice that responses after using a tool don't include an extra round of file context setup. This only affects the backend prompt logic and is live today.

ai.title: Prefer editing existing knowledge files
ai.summary: Updated prompt in `backend/src/generate-knowledge-files.ts` to instruct the model to update existing knowledge files rather than creating new ones for meaningful changes. This reduces redundancy and fragmentation in the knowledge base. The change applies to the backend knowledge generation logic.

eli5.text: The system that writes the assistant's notes now tells the assistant to update existing files instead of making new ones for the same topic, which keeps the collection of notes from getting duplicated or scattered. When the assistant writes a note, it first checks whether something on that subject already exists and, if it does, adds to that file rather than starting a new one. If you browse the notes, you'd see fewer separate files and more consolidated entries on each subject, since the system now prefers editing over creating.

ai.title: Update checkNewFilesNecessary prompt logic
ai.summary: Refined `checkNewFilesNecessary` prompt in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts`. Explicitly instructs model to identify files for modification or reading. Added fallback to display 'None' when `previousFiles` is empty.

eli5.text: The assistant now gets clearer instructions when it decides which reading materials or files to set aside before answering your request: it is explicitly told to pick files it should modify or that could help it answer you, and when there are no files already in hand, it will simply say 'None' instead of showing an empty list. This affects every conversation that triggers the file-gathering step before the assistant starts responding, so you would notice a tidier, more consistent set of files attached up front when you ask something new. It is live today for all internal backend processing of incoming requests.

ai.title: Include project file tree in knowledge file generation prompt
ai.summary: The `generateKnowledgeFiles` system prompt now injects the project file tree via `getProjectFileTreePrompt`. The previously private helper in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` was exported to allow this usage. This ensures the AI model considers the full directory structure when determining if a code change warrants a new knowledge file.

eli5.text: The system now gives the AI a full map of the project's folder structure when deciding whether a code change needs a new knowledge file. Previously the AI only saw the specific files changed, so it could miss context from the broader project layout. This affects how the backend automatically generates documentation files from code changes.
